feature: An icon's panel shows only icon rows
summary: Picking a group or a shape in an icon no longer fills the panel with page layout rows (Layout: Arrangement, Hug and Fixed, Padding, Scale; and Columns). Motion now sits right under Effects. A group on an ordinary picture keeps its Layout section.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/a-group-in-an-icon-shows-no-page-layout-walk.json.

try.do: File > New Image, pick Icon, Create.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Draw a rectangle and an oval, Shift-click both, press Command-G. The panel shows Appearance, Effects and Motion, and no Layout.
On an ordinary picture, Layer > New Frame, pick 24 under Icons, draw a rectangle inside it and pick it. No Columns, no Layout; Arrange in Frame stays.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On an ordinary picture, group two shapes. Layout is still there, under Motion.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Group the finished cloud in the whole icon workflow: the panel ends at Motion.

evaluate: With an icon group picked, is there anything you miss from the old Layout section?
Is Arrange (align in frame) still worth keeping for a shape in an icon frame?
Should Layer > Show Columns be dimmed for an icon frame, as it now is?
rough: The rule is 'everything picked is in an icon': pick one shape in an icon and one outside it and Layout comes back, because the outside one still has a page to sit on.
An icon frame picked on its own also loses Layout and Columns; its Frame section (size, clipping, surface) is untouched.
No mock covers this surface directly; none of the icon mocks draw a Layout or Columns section, so the panel now matches them more closely.
